name: What electrical and plumbing hookups should I plan for inside an RV garage?
description: Plan for a 30-amp or 50-amp dedicated outlet, high-bay lighting, standard tool receptacles, a freeze-proof hose bib, and an optional sewer dump connection.

mainEntity.name: What electrical and plumbing hookups should I plan for inside an RV garage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Planning for a dedicated 30-amp or 50-amp RV receptacle allows you to keep house batteries charged, run climate systems before trips, and power onboard equipment without draining onboard systems. Many owners also install interior LED high-bay lighting, multiple wall outlets for power tools, and an exterior hookup for visitor use. Adding a dedicated freeze-proof hose bib for washing and an integrated sewer dump station tied into your septic or municipal sewer line provides complete utility support directly inside your building.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan for a 30-amp or 50-amp dedicated outlet, high-bay lighting, standard tool receptacles, a freeze-proof hose bib, and an optional sewer dump connection.
